source.check: block image read (Irish News, 30 April 1936, p. 7, section 2.153 block 3): 'The divisions in which no nominations were received are Somerset and Drumcroon, but it is expected that the two outgoing members, Messrs. John N. Henry and Matthew Workman, respectively, will continue in office'; Matthew Workman was returned for Drumcroon in 1933

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received by Mr. S. Hezlett, clerk of the Union and returning officer, on 28 April 1936; all the outgoing councillors except two were re-nominated, and a contest was likely only in Lislea (Kilrea), where Mr. John Torrens opposed the outgoing councillor, Mr. John R. Gordon, J.P. (Irish News, 30 April 1936, p. 7; Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1936, p. 9). No nomination was received for Drumcroon, and the outgoing member, Matthew Workman, was expected to 'continue in office', that is, he was deemed re-elected. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
